evals.expected_output: The partial-context case, and the one closest to real work. Unlike evals 9 and 11 the target is NOT bare: it sits beside a README documenting usage and behaviour, a crontab fragment showing how it is invoked, a CHANGELOG, and a git history with two commits. A context search therefore SUCCEEDS and returns real material - it just never states why the thing exists or what would break without it. Constraints and Prior findings are genuinely fillable from that material, and the skill is instructed to fill every field it can before asking. Purpose is not: the README describes what the script does, which the skill's own rule says is never Purpose however accurate it is. The failure this case is built to catch is treating a found README as having answered Purpose - dispatching on a brief whose Purpose field is a behaviour summary in disguise. A blanket refusal that leaves the fillable fields empty is also wrong, and expectation 4 tests for it, so the case does not reward simply stopping on everything.
